title: step-execution.jsonl (one row per step opened and one per step closed)
description: The machine-owned execution record for one session's approved-plan steps, under .dabbler/runs/s<N>/step-execution.jsonl. Appended only by ai_router.verify. A step is in flight or it is not, and this file is what says which: the last 'opened' row with no 'closed' row after it is the open step, and there is never more than one. A row that fails validation on read is a refusal, not a skip -- an unreadable execution record means the framework cannot tell what is open, and guessing is how work escapes a plan.

schema_version.description: Frozen at v1. A reader that finds any other value refuses the record rather than interpreting it.

event.description: Two words, and no third: a step that was neither opened nor closed did not happen.

step_id.description: A step_id the session's approved plan declares. Nothing else may be opened.

base_commit.description: HEAD when the step opened. Everything the step is measured against is anchored here, so the close refuses when HEAD has moved: a commit landed mid-step and the diff no longer carries the step's work.

envelope.description: What the step changed, against what it declared. Present on 'closed'.

closed_tree.description: The worktree snapshot this step closed on, and the baseline the next step is measured against. Present on 'closed'. A closed step's work stays in the working tree until the session commits, so without this the next step would be charged for its predecessor's files -- and dropping those paths by name instead would let a later step edit them again, outside its own envelope, unremarked.

deterministic.description: The controls and the targeted test run, as facts. Present on 'closed'; a step never closes with a red required one.
